description: Inputs at the edge of the int64 / Q32 domain and the outcome every baseline must give (see domain_edges.py). Each entry changes input B of the case's fixture.

ds1000_case0438.name: wrapped_root
ds1000_case0438.why: B*C*2^64 wraps the field to t mod p < 2^126 (B, C < 2^64 not both checked): the old halo2/Noir baselines proved r = 13.72 where NumPy gives 0.0; Zinnia's domain is 1 <= B*C < 2^62

ds1000_case0438.name: variance_product_above_2_62
ds1000_case0438.why: B*C = (3 * 32768 * 21846)^2 >= 2^62: sqrt(B*C) * 2^32 leaves the Q32 window

ds1000_case0438.name: inputs_at_11585
ds1000_case0438.why: inputs within +-11585 are always inside the domain; the old zkVM programs overflowed Q32 here

ds1000_case0452.name: int64_min
ds1000_case0452.why: |i64::MIN| = 2^63 overflows int64 (NumPy wraps it); Zinnia has no proof

ds1000_case0452.name: l1_sum_overflows_int64
ds1000_case0452.why: the row's L1 norm 2^63 + 1 overflows int64 (NumPy wraps it and gives -0.5). Zinnia's int64-overflow policy is no proof; its mock and halo2-base backend currently prove 0.0 / 0.5 (a Zinnia bug, reported)

ds1000_case0452.name: l1_above_q32
ds1000_case0452.why: float(l1) = 2^40 has no Q32 code. The zkVM and Cairo programs have no result (a Q32 float(x) must exist); the halo2/Noir baselines compute floor(x * 2^32 / l1) without converting l1 and prove NumPy's value. Zinnia is inconsistent here: its halo2-base backend proves NumPy's value, its mock rejects norms just above 2^31 but returns 0.0 at 2^40 (a mock bug). Not the |i64::MIN| policy; an open question for the author.

ds1000_case0454.name: int64_min
ds1000_case0454.why: |i64::MIN| = 2^63 overflows int64 (NumPy wraps it); Zinnia has no proof

ds1000_case0454.name: linf_above_q32
ds1000_case0454.why: float(linf) = 2^40 has no Q32 code. The zkVM and Cairo programs have no result (a Q32 float(x) must exist); the halo2/Noir baselines compute floor(x * 2^32 / linf) without converting linf and prove NumPy's value. Zinnia is inconsistent here: its halo2-base backend proves NumPy's value, its mock rejects norms just above 2^31 but returns 0.0 at 2^40 (a mock bug). Not the |i64::MIN| policy; an open question for the author.

ds1000_case0322.name: int64_min
ds1000_case0322.why: np.min of i64::MIN needs no negation; the old Noir baseline negated it (-max(-a))

ds1000_case0437.name: float_min
ds1000_case0437.why: row minimum -2^31 (Q32 code i64::MIN); the old Noir baseline negated it (-max(-a))

ds1000_case0375.name: float_min
ds1000_case0375.why: the minimum grade -2^31 (Q32 code i64::MIN); the old Noir baseline negated it (-max(-grades))

ds1000_case0368.name: difference_at_min
ds1000_case0368.why: x - y has Q32 code -2^63, so |x - y| = 2^63 overflows; Zinnia has no proof

ds1000_case0368.name: reference_at_min
ds1000_case0368.why: y = -2^31 (code i64::MIN), so |y| = 2^63 overflows; Zinnia has no proof
